response.justification: The candidate has genuine geospatial experience (founded GISCollective, built GIS apps for Green Map, spoke at FOSS4G) and strong systems-level work in DLang handling millions of requests per second with low-latency async I/O, which demonstrates the distributed-systems mindset the role needs. However, his professional C++ experience is limited and dated (~6 months at National Instruments in 2014-2015), he has no Rust experience, no routing/navigation guidance background, and his recent years have been full-stack TypeScript/Node product work rather than data-pipeline engineering, making him a stretch for a C++-primary routing tiling role.
strengths: Hands-on geospatial domain experience: founded and maintains an open-source Geo-Data platform used by Green Map
Low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems work in DLang (millions of HTTP requests/sec, async I/O, fibers, caching)
Demonstrated adaptability across the stack and strong engineering practices (TDD, CI/CD, open-source contributions)
concerns: Modern C++ experience is minimal and nearly a decade old; no Rust experience listed
No experience building navigation/routing guidance systems or routing data pipelines specifically
Recent roles centered on TypeScript/Node web product development, away from systems programming
